hook.text: Slamming the brakes on ice used to mean locked wheels, no steering, and pure terror.

buildup.text: A locked wheel slides instead of rolling. Sliding tires have far less grip than rolling ones.

discovery.text: ABS uses sensors to detect which wheels are about to lock, then rapidly pulses the brakes on and off.

twist.text: It pumps the brakes up to 15 times per second—faster than any human foot could ever manage.

climax.text: The result: the tires keep rolling, you keep steering, and stopping distance shrinks on slippery roads.

punchline.text: ABS doesn't stop faster—it lets you steer while stopping.

quiz.question: What does ABS primarily help you do?
